SplitStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to split a string into several components based on
a separator. e.g: If `components` returns "1, 2, 3, 4", you could use the
", " separator to get the array ["1", "2", "3", "4"] as a result from this
formula.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string that should be split.

fields.name: separator
fields.description: The formula for the separator the string should be split on.

ElevateStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to elevate numbers to the power of other numbers.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the list of numbers that should be involved in the operation.  This list should have at least 2 numbers. The first number will be elevated to the power of the second number. If the list has more numbers in it, the result of that first operation will be elevated to the power of the third number in the list, and so on. e.g: `[2, 3, 2]` will evaluate to `64`, since `2^3 = 8` and `8^2 = 64`.

ContainsStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula returns `true` if the specified `needle` value is contained in
the `haystack`.

fields.name: haystack
fields.description: A formula returning an array (list) or string that the needle will be looked in for.

fields.name: needle
fields.description: A formula returning a value to look for in the `haystack`. It has to be a string if the haystack returns a string. Otherwise it should be of the `sub_value_type` of the array returned by `haystack`.

EnumeratedAbbreviationStatFormulaCompone.description:
This formula allows you to fetch the abbreviation for an enumerated type in
the system.

fields.name: enumerated_type
fields.description: The id for the enumerated type that you want the abbreviation for.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The formula for the id of the particular entry of the enumerated type you want the abbreviation for. Naturally, the result needs to be a valid and existing id for the specified enumerated type, or this operation will fail.

WhenClause.description: Structure to be used for the `when` stat formula clauses.

fields.name: condition
fields.description: This stat formula should evaluate to a boolean. If the condition evaluates to true, the value from `components` will be returned by the `When` formula,  provided this is the first clause whose condition evaluates to true.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula whose value should be returned if the condition is satisfied.

fields.name: clauses
fields.description: A list of conditions and associated components that should be evaluated and whose value should be returned as a value from this formula if the given condition is satisfied. Only the first clause whose condition is true will have its components evaluated and its value returned. The rest will be ignored, so the order matters. You can specify as many clauses as you want.

NotEqualsStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to check for inequality among given values. Note
that the inequality will be checked in consecutive pairs only (ie: for the
array `[1, 2, 3]`, this formula will check that `1 != 2` and that `2 != 3`,
but will NOT check if `1 != 3`). This means that this function can return
`true` even if some of the values in the array are equal (e.g:, for the
array `[1, 2, 1]`).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of values to check for inequality.

ToSignedStringStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to convert a number into a signed string (prefixed
by + or - depending on the sign of the number).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the number you want to convert to a signed string.

MultiplyStatFormulaComponent.description:
Multiplies the results of the given components. Only number (`integer` or
`decimal`) values will be multiplied.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Formula components to multiply. This formula must return an array (list) of numbers (`integer` or `decimal`).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of elements you want to map.

fields.name: mapper
fields.description: The formula for the mapping to perform on each element of the given components list.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $mapValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $mapValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the mapper.  If you were to specify the optional `map_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $mapValue to access these values.

fields.name: map_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `mapper` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `map_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `Map` formulas, as it will allow inner `Map` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

RollableStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to create a `Rollable` (as in the `rollable` value
type for stats). These type of values in the app can be used, for example,
for the `Roll` effect (under `Mechanics`).

fields.name: formulas
fields.description: The formula for the dice formulas that should be rolled and then added together. It has to return a list of strings in the form of dice formulas (see the `Roll` formula type for more details on how these formulas should look like).

fields.name: text
fields.description: A text to display next to the roll result. This is usually used to add contextual information to the roll. e.g: If rolling for damage, this might be used to keep track of the damage type that was rolled for.

SortByStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to sort an array (list) of values.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of elements you want to sort.

fields.name: sort_by_selector
fields.description: The formula for the selector that should be used to perform the sort. This selector allows you to choose a substat (if applicable) to perform the sort on. For example, if you have a list of spells and you want to sort by level, you would have the selector be:  ```json {     "type": "stat",     "stat": "$sortByValue.level" } ```  If you wanted to just sort by the value itself, you can always just write:  ```json {     "type": "stat",     "stat": "$sortByValue" } ```  Eligible selector values must be either strings or numbers, and they should all be of the same type.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $sortByValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $sortByValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the selector.  If you were to specify the optional `sort_by_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $sortByValue to access these values.

fields.name: order
fields.description: The sort order to utilize.

fields.name: sort_by_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `sort_by_selector` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `sort_by_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `SortBy` formulas, as it will allow inner `SortBy` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

ConstantStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula returns a constant value.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The constant value that this formula will return.

fields.name: value_type
fields.description: The type for the value of this formula. It has to match.

fields.name: sub_value_type
fields.description: The type of the sub value of the array this formula returns (only required if this formula returns an array and the `value_type` field is `array`).

LessThanEqualsStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to compare multiple numbers for a "less than"
relationship. e.g: Given the array of numbers [x, y, z], this formula will
return `true` if and only if x ≤ y and y ≤ z.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the values involved in the check. Has to compute to a list of numbers.

CreateChipStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows to create a `ChipRPGView`. It is most usually used for
the `ListItemRPGView` `chips` property. The chip view allows to display
either a text from a stat formula or can be provided with resource data and
automatically display resources for you in the form of text with the given
stat.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The id for the chip view. Should be unique.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Should compute to the text to be displayed on the chip. Either this property should be provided, or `resource_id`, `resource_instance_ids_stat` and `resource_display_stat` should be provided.

fields.name: background_color
fields.description: Optional. The background color for the chip. Should compute to a string for an `RPGColors` or a hex code for a color.

fields.name: border_color
fields.description: Optional. The border color for the chip. Should compute to a string for an `RPGColors` or a hex code for a color.

fields.name: style
fields.description: Optional. The style color for the chip. Should compute to a string representing a ChipRPGViewStyle. Defaults to `fullSize`.

fields.name: resource_id
fields.description: The id of the resource the chip is going to display.

fields.name: resource_instance_ids_stat
fields.description: The stat for the id or ids of resource instances that are going to be displayed in the chip. The stat has to have a string value or be an array of strings.

fields.name: resource_display_stat
fields.description: The stat of the resource that should be used to display in the chip. Most usually it's `name`.

LengthStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to query the length of a string or array (list).
e.g: if used on the list [1, 10, 11] or the string "abcde", the result of
this formula will be 3 and 5, respectively.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string or array (list) whose length you want to know.

ReplaceStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to replace a particular substring occurrence inside
another string with a given replacement.

fields.name: string
fields.description: The formula for the string where the replacements should be made

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: The formula for the substring occurrence you want to replace. The `Replace` formula _will_ replace all occurrences of this substring in the original string.

fields.name: replace
fields.description: The formula for the string that the occurrences should be replaced for.

GetStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula is, perhaps, the most important. Yet, it's also the ONLY ONE
that does not follow the pattern for formula type names. Please pay extra
attention to this, as this formula type is "stat" ((ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*･ﾟ✧) and not
"getStat" ((ʘ_ʘ)).

It allows you to fetch the value of any stat that you have access to. This
can be done directly or by providing a stat path. For example, if you have
a stat with id "spell", you could do something like "spell.name" to access
the stat "name" under the spell resource you just accessed directly.

Note that accessing a stat that doesn't exist will result in an exception (
exceptions... bad... bad exceptions... we don't want exceptions), as will
trying to access stats in a path where a previous path component was null (
e.g: in our example, if "spell" is currently null, doing "spell.name" would
throw an exception and explode, very bad stuff). To avoid this you have
several options:

1. Check the existence and non-nullability of stats with the `Defined` and
`NotNull` stat formulas in conjunction with the `When` stat formula, to
avoid trying to access things that aren't there. Or...

2. Use the conditional path character `?` in your path. When specifying a
path in this formula component, you can suffix any component of the path
with `?` (a component is anything between dots) to signal that, should that
path component be non-existent or null, the path lookup should stop and
`null` should be returned instead. So, in our previous example, we could do
"spell?.name" to prevent this from being a problem. The conditional operator
`?` is going to be your best friend in a lot of situations!

fields.name: stat
fields.description: The path to the stat you want the value of (read the beautiful explanation at the top of this page for details on syntax).

fields.name: for_resource
fields.description: Deprecated, please don't use and ignore.

fields.name: ignore_cache
fields.description: Whether the internal caching system should be circumvented when fetching this stat. This should be only used as a last resource and avoided at all costs. If you find yourself needing to use this, please contact the app developer by sending an email to feedback@blastervla.com to ensure you should be using it and this is not because of an app bug that should be fixed instead. This property has performance implications.

TrimStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to trim a string, removing any leading and trailing
whitespaces. For example, "   hello  " would turn into "hello".

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string you want to trim.

RollStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to instantly roll dice and returns the result
immediately. No UI animations will be done for this result. If you're
looking to trigger the app's dice roller and display a result, please see
the `Roll` effect under `Mechanics` instead.

fields.name: formula
fields.description: The formula for a dice roll formula. Dice roll formulas are strings in the form of "xdy + n" or "xdy - n", where x, y and n are numbers. The app will roll x dices of type dy (e.g: if y is 8, it'll roll x d8), add them up and then add (or subtract) n.

IsNullStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to check if a particular value is `null` or not. It
will return `true` if and only if the given value equals `null`.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the value you want to check for nullability.

ListStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to create a list of values.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The list of formulas to calculate the values of each element in the resulting list.

AddStatFormulaComponent.description:
Adds the results of the given components. Only number (`integer` or
`decimal`) values will be added.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Formula components to add. This formula must return an array (list) of numbers (`integer` or `decimal`).

AppendStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula takes in a formula for a list and appends the result of the
item formula to it, at the end. The item value must be of the same type as
the `sub_value_type` for the list.

fields.name: list
fields.description: The formula for the list. Must return an array (list).

fields.name: item
fields.description: The formula for the item to append to the list. The item value must be of the same type as the `sub_value_type` for the list.

fields.name: treat_as_set
fields.description: Optional. False by default. If `true`, this formula will only append the item if the list doesn't contain it yet, ensuring a duplicate isn't added. Please note that if the list already contains duplicates, it will not purge them.

EnumeratedNameStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to fetch the name for an enumerated type element in
the system.

fields.name: enumerated_type
fields.description: The id for the enumerated type that you want the name for.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The formula for the id of the particular entry of the enumerated type you want the name for. Naturally, the result needs to be a valid and existing id for the specified enumerated type, or this operation will fail.

ToNumStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to convert a string to a number.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string you want to convert to a number. If the string does not represent a valid number, this operation will fail.

EventNameStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to decorate an event name with the appropriate id
required for the event to be picked up by a particular resource. See the
`Mechanic` information banner for more context.

fields.name: event_name
fields.description: The event name to decorate.

fields.name: for_resource
fields.description: Optional. Will use the resource that this formula is being calculated on if omitted. The formula for the resource instance that the event should be executed on.

ToLowerCaseStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to turn any string into its lowercased version,
essentially converting all non-lowercase characters to lowercase.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string you want to convert to lowercase.

MetaStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to get the value of a stat whose id can be
calculated in runtime. The use of this formula should be restricted as much
as possible as overuse might result in performance issues in your system.
Use strictly where necessary. If you know the id of the stat you want to
fetch at the time of writing the system (ie: the id is static and doesn't
change at runtime), please use the `GetStat` (`stat`) formula instead.

fields.name: meta_stat
fields.description: The formula for the id of the stat whose value should be fetched. Must compute to a string for a path to an existing stat in the system. See `GetStat` for more information on paths.

DivideStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to perform an arithmetic division among numbers.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the list of numbers that should be divided. This list should have at least 2 numbers. The first number will be divided by the second number. If the list has more numbers in it, the result of that first division will be divided by the third number in the list, and so on. e.g: `[20, 2, 5]` will evaluate to `2`, since `20 / 2 = 10` and `10 / 5 = 2`.

fields.name: rounding_method
fields.description: The rounding method to be used for the operation.

JoinToStringStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to join a list of strings or numbers by a separator.
For example, if the list [1, 2, "hello", 3] is provided with a " + "
separator, the result of this formula will be the string
"1 + 2 + hello + 3".

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the list of strings or numbers that should be joined by the separator.

fields.name: separator
fields.description: The separator that should be used when joining the strings.

MinStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to get the minimum value (number) in an array
(list).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of values whose minimum value you want to get. It must return a non-empty list of numbers.

EqualsStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to check for equality among all given values.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the values involved in the equality check. Has to compute to a list. Will return `true` if and only if all the values in the list are equal. Note that 1 (the number 1) and "1" (the string for that same number) will be treated as different since they represent different things.

DefaultIfNullStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to conditionally return a default value if another
one is `null`.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the main value. If this formula returns a non-`null` value, the `DefaultIfNull` formula will return that value.

fields.name: default_components
fields.description: The formula for the default value to return in case the one in components returns a `null` value.

NegateStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula returns the negation of the given `integer` or `decimal`. ie:
If the value returned by the `components` formula is `12`, this formula will
return `-12` and vice versa.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the `integer` or `decimal` value that should be negated.

LessThanStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to compare multiple numbers for a "less than"
relationship. e.g: Given the array of numbers [x, y, z], this formula will
return `true` if and only if x < y and y < z.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the values involved in the check. Has to compute to a list of numbers.

MaxStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to get the maximum value (number) in an array
(list).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of values whose maximum value you want to get. It must return a non-empty list of numbers.

DefinedStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to query the system to check if a stat is defined or
not. If it is, it'll return `true`, and if it isn't it'll return `false`.

fields.name: stat
fields.description: The stat that you want to know is defined or not.

AndStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula will return a `bool` type that will be `true` if all the values
in `components` are `true`, and `false` otherwise. This is consistent with
Boolean algebra.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Formula components to _and_. This formula must return an array (list) of `bool` values.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of elements you want to reduce.

fields.name: reducer
fields.description: The formula for the reduction to perform on each element of the given components list. It has to be non-empty.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $reduceValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $reduceValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the reducer. It can also make use of the $reduceAccumulator value, which will have the result of executing the reducer function up to that value. Note that the first iteration will actually not execute the reducer and instead set the $reduceAccumulator to be equal to the first element.  For example, if the reducer function is just concatenating $reduceValue and $reduceAccumulator such that $reduceValue comes first, the iterations will look like this:  1. $reduceValue = 'b', $accumulatorValue = 'a', result --> `ba` 2. $reduceValue = 'c', $accumulatorValue = 'ba', result --> `cba`  If you were to specify the optional `reduce_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $reduceValue to access these values. The same goes for `reduce_accumulator_key` and $reduceAccumulator

fields.name: reduce_accumulator_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `reducer` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `reduce_accumulator_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `Reduce` formulas, as it will allow inner `Reduce` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

fields.name: reduce_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `reducer` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `reduce_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `Reduce` formulas, as it will allow inner `Reduce` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

FindFirstStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to fetch the first value in an array (list) that
satisfies a condition.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) you want to get the value from.

fields.name: filter
fields.description: The formula for the condition that the resulting value should satisfy to be returned by this `FindFirst` formula.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $findFirstValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $findFirstValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the condition.  If you were to specify the optional `find_first_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $findFirstValue to access these values.

fields.name: find_first_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `filter` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `find_first_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `FindFirst` formulas, as it will allow inner `FindFirst` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

SubtractStatFormulaComponent.description:
Subtracts the results of the given components. Only number (`integer` or
`decimal`) values will be subtracted.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Formula components to subtract. This formula must return an array (list) of numbers (`integer` or `decimal`).

FlatAppendStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to concatenate lists (also known as flattening).

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the arrays (lists) that should be concatenated.

fields.name: treat_as_set
fields.description: Optional. False by default. If `true`, this formula will remove all duplicate values from the result before returning it.

FlatMapStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula is like the `Map` formula. However, it will also flatten the
resulting list values into one. i.e: If the mapping returns three lists of
numbers, this formula will return one list flat-appending (see `FlatAppend`)
the three lists.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) of elements you want to map.

fields.name: mapper
fields.description: The formula for the mapping to perform on each element of the given components list.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $mapValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $mapValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the mapper.  If you were to specify the optional `map_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $mapValue to access these values.

fields.name: map_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `mapper` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `map_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested `FlatMap` formulas, as it will allow inner `FlatMap` formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

ToUpperCaseStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to turn any string into its uppercased version,
essentially converting all non-uppercase characters to uppercase.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the string you want to convert to uppercase.

DateStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows to format an ISO 8601 date timestamp to a MMM dd, yyyy
formatted string.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the ISO 8601 string timestamp to format.

GreaterThanEqualsStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to compare multiple numbers for a "greater than or
equals" relationship. e.g: Given the array of numbers [x, y, z], this
formula will return `true` if and only if x ≥ y and y ≥ z.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the values involved in the check. Has to compute to a list of numbers.

FilterStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to filter values from an array (list) based on a
condition.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) whose values you want to filter.

fields.name: filter
fields.description: The formula for the condition that should be satisfied for a value to be present in the array resulting from this `Filter` formula.  Anything inside this formula can make use of the $filterValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $filterValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the formula specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time as part of the condition.  If you were to specify the optional `filter_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $filterValue to access these values.

fields.name: filter_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `filter` formula to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `filter_value_key`, to make your system easier to read. This is also helpful when dealing with nested filter formulas, as it will allow inner filter formulas to access the values of outer filter formulas.

OrStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula will return a `bool` type that will be `true` if at least one
of the values in `components` is `true`, and `false` otherwise. This is
consistent with Boolean algebra.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Formula components to _or_. This formula must return an array (list) of `bool` values.

CopyResourceStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows to create a copy of a resource.

fields.name: components
fields.description: A formula returning the resource to be copied.

fields.name: preserve_ids
fields.description: If the `id` for the resource should be the same in the copy or not.

ModStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to perform an arithmetic division among numbers,
resulting in the division's remainder.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the list of numbers that should be divided and the remainder of those divisions should be returned. This list should have at least 2 numbers. The first number will be divided by the second number and the remainder of that operation will be return. If the list has more numbers in it, the result of that first operation will be divided by the third number in the list and its remainder returned, and so on. e.g: `[13, 5, 2]` will evaluate to `2`, since `13 % 5 = 3` and `3 % 2 = 1`.

fields.name: rounding_method
fields.description: The rounding method to be used for the underlying division operation.

IsEmptyStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to check if an array (list) or a string is empty. It
will return `true` if and only if the list or string is empty.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the array (list) or string you want to check the emptiness of.

NotStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula returns the negation of the given `bool`. ie: If the `bool`
value returned by the `components` formula is `true`, this formula will
return `false` and vice versa.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the `bool` value that should be negated.

GreaterThanStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to compare multiple numbers for a "greater than"
relationship. e.g: Given the array of numbers [x, y, z], this formula will
return `true` if and only if x > y and y > z.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the values involved in the check. Has to compute to a list of numbers.

ConcatStatFormulaComponent.description: This formula allows you to concatenate strings and numbers.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The components to concatenate. Must compute to an array (list) of strings and/or numbers. If numbers are in the array they will automatically be converted to strings to concatenate.  e.g: If components computes to `["STR: ", 18, " (+", 4, ")"]`, the result will be "STR: 18 (+4)".

NotNullStatFormulaComponent.description:
This formula allows you to check if a particular value is `null` or not. It
will return `true` if and only if the given value is not equal to `null`.

This formula is equivalent to composing a `Not` formula with a `IsNull`
formula.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The formula for the value you want to check for nullability.

PopUpButtonRPGView.description:
This view will display as a button. Upon tapping on the button, a pop-up
will be triggered. You can customize the pop-up view as you like.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: text
fields.description: A formula for the text to display in the button. Either this property or `icon` need to be provided.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: The icon to display in the button. It has to be an `Icon` view. Trying to display a non-icon view will simply not work.

fields.name: pop_up_view
fields.description: The `RPGView` to be displayed as content for the pop up.

fields.name: pop_up_title
fields.description: The title for the pop up. This stat formula must compute to a string.

fields.name: pop_up_type
fields.description: Optional. The type for the pop up. If not specified, it will default to bottom sheet.

fields.name: display_cancel_button
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to true. Whether to display a cancel button or not.

fields.name: cancel_text
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to a stat formula that returns "Cancel". A stat formula returning a string to display as text in the cancel button.

fields.name: display_save_button
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to false. Whether to display a save button or not. If this is false but a `save_text` is provided, the text will override this value and the save button will display.

fields.name: save_text
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to a stat formula that returns "Save". A stat formula returning a string to display as text in the save button.

fields.name: should_persist_on_save
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to false. Whether or not the given resource should be persisted (saved in the database) upon saving. You would want to set this to true if you are editing a first-level resource. However, if you are editing (for example) a resource within a resource within the character (e.g: an effect, which is in an item, which is in the `items` stat in the character), you would want to set it as `false`, as you would want to allow the user to finish editing the whole resource before saving (as they might regret their choices and choose to exit without saving to discard their changes).

fields.name: extra_buttons
fields.description: Optional. This allows you to specify an array of buttons to display at the bottom of the pop up.

fields.name: in_edit_mode
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to false. If the alert should be in edit mode by default. This might be particularly helpful if you are using it to display `Stat` `RPGView`s and want to allow the user to edit them.

fields.name: dismissible
fields.description: Optional. Indicates if the alert should be dismissible by tapping outside of it. If not provided, it will default to dismissible if there is no save button nor save button text specified, and it will default to non-dismissible if there is to prevent the user from accidentally dismissing a sheet in which they were working.

SelectRPGView.description:
This view allows the player to select one or multiple options from an array
of pre-approved selections.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: stat
fields.description: Either this property or `meta_stat` has to be provided. The path to the `stat` that this view pulls its selected value from (and updates the selected value on). This path can use the syntax for paths defined in the `GetStat` stat formula. The stat has to be of the `string` type.

fields.name: meta_stat
fields.description: Either this property or `stat` has to be provided. A formula for the path to the stat that this view pulls its selected value from (and updates the selected value on). Only use this property if the actual stat id will change in runtime. Otherwise, use the `stat` property, as this one will have performance implications for your system.

fields.name: options
fields.description: Either this property or `resource_options` should be provided. The `id` of the enumerated type containing the options that should be available for the player to choose from. Alternatively, it could be the `id` of a core resource in the app (don't forget to also provide `options_display_stat` if so). This will cause all the resource instances of that particular resource to be displayed as options.

fields.name: allowed_options
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to all options. A stat formula for a list of string ids, corresponding to the options from the given enumerated type that you want to be displayed for the user as eligible options.

fields.name: resource_options
fields.description: Either this property or `resource_options` should be provided. A formula returning the resource instances that the player can choose from.

fields.name: max_selection_amount
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to nothing (ie: unlimited). Only works when `multi_select` is `true`. A formula computing to an integer representing the maximum amount of options that the player can select.

fields.name: options_display_stat
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to the `display_name` of the resource (or "name" if `display_name` is undefined for the given resource). Needs to be set if a resource id is given as the value for `options`.

fields.name: multi_select
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Whether or not this view should allow multiple selections or not.

fields.name: style
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `dropdown`. The style of the view.

fields.name: resource_saved_stat
fields.description: Optional. Only applies when `options` references a resource id or `resource_options` is used. The stat of the resource whose value should be saved to the linked `stat` when the player makes a selection. Defaults to the resource instance id.

fields.name: should_auto_save
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. This flag indicates if any change to the control's state should automatically be saved for the resource / character, without giving the player the option to choose if they want to save or not.

TextRPGView.description:
Values in descending order based on their associated text size.
This view allows you to display texts and/or allow the user to input text
into a field. This field will behave different in edit mode!

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Either `text`, `edit_stat` or both properties need to be provided. Alternatively, you could also provide the resource properties instead of either of these two.  The formula for the text to display. If only `text` is provided, this text will display all the time. If `edit_stat` is also provided, this text will only display when not in edit mode, as going into edit mode will cause the `edit_stat` to display in a text field that the user can edit.

fields.name: edit_stat
fields.description: Either `text`, `edit_stat` or both properties need to be provided. Alternatively, you could also provide the resource properties instead of either of these two.  The stat to modify when the value of this text field changes. If only `edit_stat` is provided, this view will display and behave as a text field all the time. If `text` is also provided, this text field will only display when in edit mode, as while in non-edit mode the `text` will be displayed as a regular label.

fields.name: style
fields.description: The style for the text. This style comprises both text size as well as flair.

fields.name: max_lines
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null` (no guarantees made that the text will display fully if it goes to multiple lines). The maximum amount of lines that the text can have. The rest will be truncated. The edit mode text field is unaffected by this property.

fields.name: max_length
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null`. Only relevant for edit mode or `edit_stat`.  The maximum length of the string value that the player inputs in the text field. This length will be used to automatically size the height of the text field. If `null`, the length will be deemed unlimited. Whenever possible, specify length as it will make the control size display more accurately for the player, and it will also act as a form of validation in your system.

fields.name: signed
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Only relevant when the `edit_stat` is a number (`integer` or `decimal`). This will determine if the view should allow the player to type in negative numbers or not.

fields.name: hint
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null` (no hint). Only relevant for edit mode (with `edit_stat`). A placeholder text that will display in the text field. Often used for default values, but can also be used to hint the player with an example of the type of value that should be in the field.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null` (no hint). Only relevant for edit mode (with `edit_stat`). A label that should clarify what the field is for. If used, the text field will have a surrounding box. For more compact fields, consider only using `hint` instead.

fields.name: bold
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Only affects the `text` property (ie: non-edit mode). Whether or not the text should be displayed in bold.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to the `textColor` of the color scheme selected by the user. Should compute be a string for an `RPGColors` or a hex code for a color that will be used for the text (either in the label for `text` or the text field for `edit_stat`).

fields.name: markdown
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Only relevant for non-edit mode (ie: when only `text` is provided with no `edit_stat`, or when the view is not currently in edit mode). When `true`, the text will be rendered as Markdown. The rendering is gated on whether the resolved text actually contains Markdown markup; plain text is always rendered with the standard text widget regardless of this flag.  Notes: - `max_lines` is ignored when `markdown: true`. - `bold` is ignored when `markdown: true`; use Markdown `**bold**` syntax   instead. - Has no effect when displaying resource names (`resource_id` mode).

fields.name: resource_id
fields.description: You can provide the 3 resource properties instead of `text` or `edit_stat`. These will allow you to display resources as text. The `resource_id` corresponds to the id of the type of resource (in your system) that you want to display in this field.

fields.name: resource_instance_ids_stat
fields.description: The path to the stat containing the list (or single) resource ids you want to show in this text label. These ids should correspond to the type of resource specified in `resource_id`.

fields.name: resource_display_stat
fields.description: The stat of the resource that should be displayed in this text label. Most likely `name` or something along those lines.

ResourceSectionRPGView.description:
This view allows you to display a series of resources (only the
`list_view`). Each of these resources will display the `display_view` if the
user taps it (unless specified otherwise), and it also offers the
possibility to remove resources by swiping them to one side of the screen.
This is particularly useful to display arrays of resources in the character
sheet.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: header_view
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to nothing. A view to display at the top of the section, before the list of resources.

fields.name: resource_stat
fields.description: The path to the stat that contains the resource instances to display. This path can use the syntax for paths defined in the `GetStat` stat formula. The stat has to be an array of resources.

fields.name: resource_set_stat
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null`. The path to the stat that should be affected when removing items from this list of resources. If not specified, the `resource_stat` property will be used. This is useful when you are showing a calculated stat with a combined list of resources from different substats, and deletion/edits should only remove stats from a "user" resource array (base, not computed) stat. You should always avoid setting calculated stats with this type of view, as the calculated stat will be overridden and will never calculate its value again. Also, see the `read_only` property.

fields.name: resource_id
fields.description: The resource id for the type of resources being displayed (ie: the one defined in your resource within the system file).

fields.name: read_only
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Whether or not this view is read-only. If so, it will not allow deletions of resources, nor edits while viewing their `display_view`s. Again, similar to the explanation in `resource_set_stat`, if you are displaying a computed stat array in this list and are NOT going to make this view `read_only`, you should define a `resource_set_stat` with the base stat that contains the resources the user might be deleting or editing.

fields.name: tap_displays_resource
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `true`. Whether tapping on a resource should display its `display_view` in a bottom sheet or not.

fields.name: content_item_min_width
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to nothing (no constraints enforced). The minimum width for an item in this list. If the number is a fraction (ie: between 0 (exclusive) and 1 (inclusive)) it will be taken as a fraction of the screen size (e.g: 1 is the full screen width, 0.5 is half the screen width, etc). This is useful for responsive layouts. If the number is above 1, it will be treated as an absolute number for the width.

fields.name: alignment
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `center`. The alignment to use for the elements in the list.

fields.name: max_items_in_preview
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null`. If set, this property allows to define a maximum number of items that should show in a `preview` of the full list, which will be accessible through a button at the bottom of the preview. If `null` (unset), the full list will be displayed directly inline instead.

fields.name: reorganizable
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. If set to true, items in this section can be reordered via drag and drop. When enabled, moving an item updates and saves the underlying stat order.

SelectResourcesRPGView.description:
Controls whether inline resource creation (via EditResourcePage) is offered.

- `disabled`: existing behaviour — core resources open the compendium,
  non-core / `createInPlace` resources open the existing inline popup.
- `optional`: the tap shows a menu letting the user choose between
  "Select from compendium" and "Create new".
- `only`: the tap goes straight to inline creation (EditResourcePage).
This view allows the player to select or create a resource and assign it as
the value for a stat.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: stat
fields.description: The path to the stat that should be linked (edited) by this view. It has to be a stat with `value_type` = `resource`, or an array of resources.

fields.name: resource_id
fields.description: The id for the resource that this view handles. This is the id of the resource in your system file, NOT the id of an instance of a resource.

fields.name: preserve_ids
fields.description: Optional, defaults to `false`. Whether the resources selected should preserve their original resource ids or not.

fields.name: view_type
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `list`. The style with which this view should display. `list` will display as a button and will show the name of the resource that was selected. `icon` will simply display as a `+` icon. The `icon` `view_type` is usually used in conjunction with the `should_append` field and is particularly useful for resource sections.

fields.name: should_append
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. This property is only relevant for when the linked `stat` is an array of resources. When it is `true`, selecting a new resource will only append it to the list. This is powerful but means that, unless you provide another way to remove resources from this list (e.g: by using the `ResourceSection` view in conjunction with this), the player won't be able to remove resources. Having this flag be `false` will cause all the contents of the array to be replaced by the new selection/s.

fields.name: should_save_on_selection
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. Whether or not this view should automatically save as soon as a selection is made. Combine with the `should_append` flag and the `icon` view type, as well as the `ResourceSection` view to allow the player to add new resources to their list of resources (e.g: for a list of equipment items, spells, etc).

fields.name: create_in_place
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. If this flag is `true`, it will allow the player to create a new resource in place (by use of a pop-up) instead of having the player choose from existing resources.  Note: If a non-core resource is provided in `resource_id`, this flag will be forced `true` as there's no way for a player to choose a non-core resource.

fields.name: creation_pop_up_type
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `bottomSheet`. The type of pop-up that should be used when creating in place.

fields.name: filters
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to an empty map. A map of preselected filters that should be used when allowing the player to choose their existing resource/s. The keys of the map should correspond to the `stat` property of existing filters (defined in the system) for that particular resource, and the values should be stat formulas that should compute to an appropriate value for that filter (e.g: if the stat is `name`, a string stat, then the formula should compute to a string).

fields.name: inline_creation_mode
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `disabled`. Controls whether the player can create a resource inline (via a full-screen edit page) instead of, or in addition to, selecting from the compendium.  - `disabled` — existing behaviour (compendium for core resources,   in-place popup for non-core / `create_in_place` resources). - `optional` — a menu is shown on tap, letting the player choose between   "Select from compendium" and "Create new". - `only` — always opens the full-screen edit page for inline creation.

ButtonRPGView.description: This view allows you to fire an event when the user taps it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: text
fields.description: A formula for the button's text. Must return a string.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to the `true` constant. A formula to signal if the button is enabled or not. A disabled button does nothing when pressed and will show greyed out.

fields.name: event_names

Each of these event names require you to make  use of the `eventName` stat formula component where appropriate to ensure the events get picked up by the appropriate resource (for clarification, see the information banner in `Mechanic`).

fields.name: event
fields.description: Optional. Either this property or `event_names` should be provided. The event that should be fired when this button is pressed.

StatRPGView.description:
This view is going to be, most likely, a staple in your character sheet
design. As the name implies, it's designed to directly display stats within
your sheet, with as little extra details as required. Be sure to read
through all the properties of this one, it's a mighty one!

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for the view. You can use it to reference view values in stat formulas by doing `$view.view_id` (where `view_id` is the id that was assigned to this view by you in the system definition)

fields.name: margin_left
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the left of this view.

fields.name: margin_right
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the right of this view.

fields.name: margin_top
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the top of this view.

fields.name: margin_bottom
fields.description: Optional. How much margin to add to the bottom of this view.

fields.name: is_visible
fields.description: Optional. A formula to specify if the view should be visible or not. Must return a bool.

fields.name: validation_message
fields.description: Optional. If this view is an input, you can define this formula to return a message when the input value is invalid. If the input is valid, you should return `null`. Otherwise, make the formula return the string that should be shown to the user.

fields.name: stat
fields.description: The path to the stat that will display in this stat. Be wary that the name that will display in this view is the name of this stat!

fields.name: edit_stat
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `null`. Sometimes you'll want to display the value of one stat but have the player edit a different one when in edit mode (e.g: you might want to display an ability modifier, but when editing you would want the player to edit the ability score instead). This is exactly what this property is here for.

fields.name: change_amount
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to 1. When in edit mode, number stats will have an up and down arrow to edit the value. The `change_amount` determines how much a single tap on an arrow increments or decrements the value of the stat. If set to `0`, this stat will NOT be editable by the user (ie: the app will not display the up and down arrow buttons).

fields.name: min_value_allowed
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to no minimum. The minimum value that this stat should be allowed to take. Only relevant for number stats.

fields.name: max_value_allowed
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to no maximum. The maximum value that this stat should be allowed to take. Only relevant for number stats.

fields.name: calculated_min_value_allowed
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to no minimum. Analogous to `min_value_allowed`, but allows you to calculate this value in runtime instead. This formula should compute to a valid number. If both this property and `min_value_allowed` are provided, the latter will take precedence.

fields.name: calculated_max_value_allowed
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to no maximum. Analogous to `max_value_allowed`, but allows you to calculate this value in runtime instead. This formula should compute to a valid number. If both this property and `max_value_allowed` are provided, the latter will take precedence.

fields.name: on_tap_event
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to none. The event that should be fired when the player taps on this stat. Can be useful to, for example, trigger dice rolls.

fields.name: on_long_tap_event
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to none. The event that should be fired when the player long-taps (long-presses) on this stat. Be wary, though, as including this property will not allow the user to enter into edit mode directly by long-pressing on this stat.

fields.name: bottom_sheet_view
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to no view. If a view is provided here, the app will display this view as a bottom sheet when the user taps on the stat. This will be ignored if you have provided an `on_tap_event`.

fields.name: bottom_sheet_in_edit_mode
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to `false`. If a `bottom_sheet_view` was provided, this flag will determine if that bottom sheet should start in edit mode or not.

fields.name: sheet_title
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to an empty string. Should be provided if a `bottom_sheet_view` is provided. The value of this formula will be used as the title for the sheet.

fields.name: stat_color
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to the textColor for the color scheme selected by the user. Should compute be a string for an `RPGColors` or a hex code for a color that will be used as the color for the stat value.

fields.name: name_color

The Delayed effect is used to delay the execution of the child effect by a
given amount of time (in milliseconds).

ForEachEffect.description:
The for each effect allows you to iterate over an array and perform an
effect (`apply`) for each of its values.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The array of values to iterate on. This stat formula must return an array.

fields.name: apply
fields.description: The effect to apply to each of the values in the `components` array. Anything inside this effect can make use of the $forEachValue stat, which will contain the current value for the iteration (e.g: if iterating the array ['a', 'b', 'c'], $forEachValue will first be equal to 'a', then 'b' and then 'c'), thus allowing the effect specified here to access the value of each element in the array one at a time.  If you were to specify the optional `for_each_value_key` parameter, you should use the key given there instead of $forEachValue to access these values.

fields.name: for_each_value_key
fields.description: Optional parameter that lets you provide a key to use in the `apply` effect to access the array's current value in the iteration. e.g: if you are iterating classes, you might want to assign "$class" to the `for_each_value_key`, to make your system easier to read.

fields.name: synchronous
fields.description: Optional parameter (true by default) to indicate if iteration should be done synchronously. If so, the app will wait until the apply function completes before continuing with the next value in the array.  For example, if the apply function displays a pop up (by using the `showPopUp` effect), it will wait until the pop up is dismissed before carrying on with the next element in the array.  Setting this to `false` will execute the apply effect for all values simultaneously.

ShowPopUpEffect.description:
This effect allows you to display a pop up to the user in the form of an
alert or a bottom sheet. An alert displays as a floating pop up, and the
bottom sheet is presented from the bottom of the screen much like resources
do in the app.

fields.name: pop_up_title
fields.description: The title for the pop up. This stat formula must compute to a string.

fields.name: pop_up_type
fields.description: Optional. The type for the pop up. If not specified, it will default to bottom sheet.

fields.name: display_cancel_button
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to true. Whether to display a cancel button or not.

fields.name: cancel_text
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to a stat formula that returns "Cancel". A stat formula returning a string to display as text in the cancel button.

fields.name: display_save_button
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to false. Whether to display a save button or not. If this is false but a `save_text` is provided, the text will override this value and the save button will display.

fields.name: save_text
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to a stat formula that returns "Save". A stat formula returning a string to display as text in the save button.

fields.name: should_persist_on_save
fields.description: Optional. Defaults to false. Whether or not the given resource should be persisted (saved in the database) upon saving. You would want to set this to true if you are editing a first-level resource. However, if you are editing (for example) a resource within a resource within the character (e.g: an effect, which is in an item, which is in the `items` stat in the character), you would want to set it as `false`, as you would want to allow the user to finish editing the whole resource before saving (as they might regret their choices and choose to exit without saving to discard their changes).

If not provided, it will default to dismissible if there is no save button nor save button text specified, and it will default to non-dismissible if there is to prevent the user from accidentally dismissing a sheet in which they were working.

This effect allows you to execute multiple effects, one after the other, in
sequence.

fields.name: effects

fields.description: Optional parameter (true by default) to indicate if iteration should be done synchronously. If so, the app will wait until an effect is complete before continuing with the next effect in the given array of effects.  For example, if the current effect displays a pop up (by using the `showPopUp` effect), it will wait until the pop up is dismissed before carrying on with the next effect in the sequence.  Setting this to `false` will execute all the effects simultaneously.

This effect allows you to specify branches in your system, enabling you to
perform different effects depending on the conditions you specify and the

This effect allows you to show a message to the user in the form of a banner

This effect allows you to trigger the app's dice roller functionality, to
roll dice and display the result.

SetStatEffect.description:
This effect allows you to set the value of a particular stat. If manually
adding to the stat value, consider using `addToStat` instead (you will find
an extensive example in its documentation). `setStat` will utilize value
overrides as opposed to modifier overrides (which `addToStat` would use
instead).

fields.name: stat
fields.description: Stat to affect. Either `stat` or `meta_stat` need to be present. If both are present, `stat` will take priority.

fields.name: meta_stat
fields.description: Stat to affect. Either `stat` or `meta_stat` need to be present. If both are present, `stat` will take priority. `meta_stat` should only be used if the stat to affect needs to be calculated in runtime, as it impacts app performance. This stat formula must return a string.

fields.name: new_value
fields.description: The formula for the value that the stat should be set to. The value this stat formula returns must have the same type as the one declared in the `value_type` (and `sub_value_type`, if appropriate) for the stat specified in `stat` or `meta_stat`.

fields.name: aggregation_type
fields.description: The aggregation type for the override resulting from the execution of this effect. See `AggregationType` for more details. If both `aggregation_type` and `calculated_aggregation_type` are omitted, the override will use `none` as the default aggregation type.

fields.name: calculated_aggregation_type
fields.description: To be used when the aggregation type should be calculated in runtime. Otherwise, use `aggregation_type`. If `aggregation_type` is also defined, this property will be ignored. This stat formula must return a string value matching one of the `AggregationType` values.

ForwardEventEffect.description:
This effect allows you to forward a received event, changing its name but
retaining its payload.

fields.name: new_event_names
fields.description: The event names to forward this event as. This stat formula should return a list of strings. As with the `fireEvent` effect, you are responsible for utilizing the `eventName` stat formula component where appropriate to ensure the events get picked up by the appropriate resource (for clarification, see the information banner in `Mechanic`).  The event will be forwarded _n_ times, where _n_ is the size of the array returned by this stat formula, once for every event name present in it.  Only the event name will be changed when forwarding. The payload will remain as is.

AddToStatEffect.description:
This effect allows you to add to the value of a particular stat. Even though
you could always use the `setStat` effect instead by manually adding to the
value to set, it is always recommended to use this effect for additions
(or subtractions) as this will set a modifier override as opposed to a value
override. Modifier overrides will act separate from value overrides and are
most likely what you want.

For example, let's say that a player with intelligence = 10 equips two
items. The first item adds one adds 1 to their intelligence, and the player
then equips a second item that sets their intelligence to 20. There are two
potential outcomes:

1. The intelligence is 21
2. The intelligence is 20

If you'd want the app to behave as in (1), then you'd want to use an
`addToStat` effect for the first item, and a `setStat` effect for the second
one. This way, the modifier (+1) will always be applied, regardless of if
the stat is later modified in other ways.

If you want the app to behave as (2), then you want to use `setStat` (and
use a `max` aggregation type).

Finally, remember that modifier overrides only clash with modifier
overrides, and value overrides only clash with value overrides. This means
that, going back to the previous example, if the player equips another item
that adds a +3 to their intelligence, the first item and the last will
clash, and which modifier/s prevail will depend on the aggregation type (for
aggregation type `max`, the +3 will prevail, for `min` the +1, for `sum`
we'll end up with a +4, etc). If the +1 was set with an aggregation type
that is different from the one used in the effect that added the +3, then
the user will be prompted to see how they want to choose to resolve the
clash.

fields.name: stat
fields.description: Stat to affect. Either `stat` or `meta_stat` need to be present. If both are present, `stat` will take priority.

fields.name: meta_stat
fields.description: Stat to affect. Either `stat` or `meta_stat` need to be present. If both are present, `stat` will take priority. `meta_stat` should only be used if the stat to affect needs to be calculated in runtime, as it impacts app performance. This stat formula must return a string.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The formula for the value that should be added to the stat. The value this stat formula returns must have the same type as the one declared in the `value_type` (and `sub_value_type`, if appropriate) for the stat specified in `stat` or `meta_stat`.

fields.name: aggregation_type
fields.description: The aggregation type for the override resulting from the execution of this effect. See `AggregationType` for more details. If both `aggregation_type` and `calculated_aggregation_type` are omitted, the override will use `none` as the default aggregation type.

fields.name: calculated_aggregation_type
fields.description: To be used when the aggregation type should be calculated in runtime. Otherwise, use `aggregation_type`. If `aggregation_type` is also defined, this property will be ignored. This stat formula must return a string value matching one of the `AggregationType` values.

DismissResourceEffect.description:
The Dismiss effect dismisses the bottom sheet displaying a particular
resource. It will dismiss the resource to which this effect is attached,
unless the `id` parameter is specified.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional parameter which allows to signal the id of the resource that should be dismissed. If that resource is not being displayed, nothing will happen. This stat formula must return a string.

Mechanic.description:
A Mechanic is, as the name implies, a functional piece of your RPG system.
Mechanics represent things that your RPG system does, such as rolling dice,
displaying resources, modifying character stats or running other mechanics
(I bet you didn't see that one coming!).

Mechanics are mainly composed of effects. In fact, a mechanic can only do
things through effects.

Every resource (and character) definition can contain mechanics, but these
mechanics will only run within the context of a character sheet. This means
that a mechanic will not run when editing a resource (say, editing a Spell),
even if the Spell resource you defined in the system includes that mechanic.
However, if the player is in the character sheet, and the character has a
Spell as a value of one of its stats, that mechanic will be active while the
player is in the character sheet.

To continue with this example, you might want to add a mechanic to a Spell
so that the app rolls damage when the player tries to cast it.

Another potential mechanic use in a resource is to equip or unequip an
armor, for example:

<details>
  <summary>Example mechanic to toggle armor equip status</summary>
```json
{
    "id": "armor_equip",
    "event_names": "toggle_equip",
    "effects": {
        "type": "when",
        "clauses": [
            {
                "condition": {
                    "type": "stat",
                    "stat": "is_equipped"
                },
                "effect": {
                    "type": "setStat",
                    "stat": "$character.equipped_armor_id",
                    "new_value": {
                        "type": "constant",
                        "value": "",
                        "value_type": "string"
                    },
                    "aggregation_type": "set"
                }
            },
            {
                "condition": {
                    "type": "constant",
                    "value": true,
                    "value_type": "bool"
                },
                "effect": {
                    "type": "setStat",
                    "stat": "$character.equipped_armor_id",
                    "new_value": {
                        "type": "stat",
                        "stat": "id"
                    },
                    "aggregation_type": "set"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```
</details>

Notice how the mechanic defines a comma-separated list of event names. These
event names will be the ones that trigger the mechanic. Events can be fired
in a number of ways in the RPG Companion App, such as the `Button` view, or
even the `FireEvent` effect. This means a mechanic could potentially trigger
other mechanics.

:::info

Event names for mechanics _can_ get tricky when trying to trigger mechanics
by firing events from other resources. Internally, mechanics append a unique
id to their event names in runtime to ensure that if you have multiple
mechanics using the same event names simultaneously (e.g: multiple spell
resource instances) they don't get triggered by accident. It would be pretty
bad if the player tried to cast one spell and ended up casting all of them!

As a rule of thumb, whenever you're typing an event name directly (ie:
**not** in a stat formula like "constant", for example), the appropriate id
will be appended for you automatically. However, if you use a stat formula (
such as for the `event_names` property of the `FireEvent` effect), you are
responsible with curating that event name. You can use the `EventName` stat
formula component to achieve this easily (you DO NOT need to use EventName
when defining `calculated_event_names` or `calculated_revert_event_names`
for a mechanic, just when you want to fire it).

A scenario in which you would want to do the latter on purpose, for example,
is if you're trying to trigger a mechanic by firing an event from a
different resource mechanic or view.

:::

Finally, mechanics can have revert event names. If provided, whenever one of
the events listed is fired the mechanic will undo (ahem... revert) all
reversible effects (e.g: `setStat`, `addToStat`, etc).

The RPG Companion App has some special events called `Lifecycle events` (see
`Character Sheet Lifecycle`).

Phew! That was a handful!
